subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw initially accept only canonical core readiness conditions and compatibility projections, or commit now to the full provider, hosting-profile, CLI, artifact-identity, and release-conformance contract?
rationale: Neither current main nor the draft implementation determines which permanent availability, configuration, plugin API, CLI, and support promises maintainers intend to own.

options.title: Accept a staged foundation
options.body: Approve core conditions and legacy-compatible projections first, then require separate acceptance and proof for providers, profiles, CLI, artifact identity, and release conformance.

options.title: Accept the full contract
options.body: Approve all proposed surfaces after the RFC lifecycle, implementation defects, conflicts, and packaged fresh-install and upgrade proof are complete.

options.title: Keep hosting composition external
options.body: Retain the fixed Gateway readiness contract and leave hosting-specific composition to host or plugin integrations.

recommendation.title: Accept a staged foundation
recommendation.body: Approve core conditions and legacy-compatible projections first, then require separate acceptance and proof for providers, profiles, CLI, artifact identity, and release conformance.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history directly connects this person to RFC acceptance policy, with runtime owners available for the technical contract review.
